title: The Witness
subtitle: Truth & Revelation

lore.description:
The Witness preserves what happened after everyone with power has agreed on another account. Her followers keep the torn letter, remember who stood at the door, and learn the names omitted from the public memorial. Her gifts make evidence difficult to bury; they do not decide whom it is wise to tell. The faithful must live with knowledge they cannot comfortably forget, including truths that expose their own part in a wrong. Some become relentless accusers. Others keep a testimony safe until its speaker can survive being heard.

**The copy that an office did not order.**

Ecktoria's Ink-Eye is invoked by clerks whose work survives the officials directing it. A private copy can begin as a safeguard against being blamed for a superior's instruction. Descendants may inherit it as evidence of a crime the family has never dared name. Some keepers defend the copy because they want public truth; others because they want the person who dictated it to remain aware that it exists.

The Witness's congregations learned to exchange testimony across institutional boundaries when an office could suppress what remained inside it. The practice preserved vulnerable speakers. It also created opportunities for an ambitious keeper to decide which disclosure would damage a rival most. Accurate evidence does not settle the keeper's motives.

**The Fractured Mirror in Vhasia.**

Vhasian Fractured Mirror observances developed around retinues whose members were expected to preserve the honor of a house. A servant who saw a lord keep one oath and violate another might possess the only account that could explain a later feud. Some households keep a covered mirror at the place testimony is received; others break the old frame when the witness who used it dies.

Marriage carried those observances between rival courts. The same testimony can survive in two family histories with different passages emphasized. An investigator who wants the whole account may have to persuade a witness's descendants that their ancestor's loyalty can survive an admission of what they actually saw.

**Names beside the lamps.**

Pereshi Keepers of the Pure Flame approach the Witness with the Oath of Flame & Light while preserving texts and tending lamps. Their work is devotional even when the copied material concerns a disputed field rather than a miracle. The Ash-Readers' challenge to orthodox practice has made some copies particularly difficult to preserve openly. A Keeper may consider an argument dangerous and still refuse to destroy the record that it was made.

In Zakov's Salt-Fire, the Witness and the Pale Shepherd are invoked by the Namers over the Roll of the Drowned. One preserves who was lost; the other accompanies passage. The work can expose a shipowner who reported cargo carefully and passengers incompletely. A Sidhi lighthouse community may share names with the Namers without adopting their doctrine of the sea.

**A witness is not an entire archive.**

Sihai's official examinations reward a defensible account, and the Witness can be approached by someone who knows the accepted account omits a living person. Lethai-thora keepers preserve knowledge at a cost to their own memories; invoking the Witness does not restore their entire lost history or make every archive infallible. A copied statement and a person who remembers it remain different kinds of evidence.

The Apocalyptic Witness's belief that final disclosure will end the world belongs to that cult. It is not the narrator's explanation of the setting. Let its members produce something true and then disagree with others about whether publishing it now protects the speaker. A survivor asking that a testimony remain sealed can confront the congregation with a harder duty than exposing one more powerful liar. Truthful preservation and immediate public revelation are not the same act.
lore.followers: Among the peoples of Fate's Edge, the Witness is known by many names. In Ecktoria, she is the Ink-Eye, the Censor's clerk who copies every redacted line onto a private scroll. In Vhasia, she is the Fractured Mirror, prayed to by spies who seek to reveal a rival's true loyalty. In the Mistlands, she is the Fog-Scribe, whose name is whispered when a bell line fails and the dead must be identified by their secrets. And in the shadows of every great city, there are those who follow the Apocalyptic Witness—a doomsaying cult that believes the world will end when the last hidden truth is finally spoken aloud, and who work to hasten that revelation by exposing every lie, no matter the cost.
signs: A scrap of parchment with a name you recognise, found where you least expect it
A sudden, vivid memory of a lie you told years ago
A sense that you are being watched by something that does not blink
quotes: "I will show you what you would rather forget. But first, you must forget what you think you know."
"Truth is not a gift. It is a burden. Carry it well, or it will crush you."
"When all that is hidden is seen, the world will either break or be free. We will be there to witness which."

domain_focus: Truth Revelation: exposing lies, uncovering secrets, forcing confessions
Memory Keeping: preserving knowledge, recalling forgotten facts
Inconvenient Knowledge: learning what others wish to hide
Prophetic Warning: seeing the consequences of hidden truths
Burden of Witness: the psychological weight of knowing too much

thiasos.description: The Witness's Thiasos is a small creature that embodies memory and revelation: a raven that collects shiny objects and recites forgotten names, a silverfish that eats lies from parchment and leaves truth behind, a small brass beetle whose shell opens to reveal a perfect mirror, a white mouse that nests in archive drawers and remembers every page it has slept upon, or a cricket that chirps in the key of the last secret spoken nearby.
thiasos.care: Beyond its ordinary care, this Thiasos must witness something significant (a lie told, a secret revealed, a confession made) each week. If that need goes unmet, the Thiasos becomes Compromised: it grows silent and still, and its bearer loses +1 die on all Investigation rolls until it is shown a hidden truth.

codex.description: A Codex sworn to the Witness is never a book that can be closed. It may be a set of loose leaf pages that reorganise themselves each dawn, a scroll that writes itself when no one is looking, a chalkboard that cannot be erased, or a stack of wax tablets that melt and reset each season.
codex.upkeep: Because the Witness values accuracy over permanence, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week correcting a single error in its records (a misspelled name, a misdated event) or the Rites stored there become garbled (treat as Compromised until restored).

patrons_gift.name: Word of Truth
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of the Witness may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or writing implement) and whisper a word of truth.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Insight or Investigation rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would be deceived by an illusion or a lie, they may roll twice and take the better result.
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to the Witness.

rites.name: Rite of the Lingering Trace
rites.materials: A trace of the thing to be remembered (hair, dust, a spoken name).
rites.effect: You follow a hidden thread. Gain +1 die to investigate or notice something directly related to the trace within the current scene. Additionally, you may ask the GM one yes/no question about whether the trace is connected to a specific person, event, or object.
rites.push_it: Gain +2 dice instead, but mark 1 segment on a Memory Strain Timer [4]. If the timer fills, you gain Fatigue 1 and suffer –1 die on Investigation/Notice rolls until the end of the next scene (the Witness taxes your mind). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Uncomfortable Question
rites.materials: A circle drawn with chalk or string while focusing on a specific person.
rites.effect: You force a moment of raw honesty. Ask one question of a target within the zone. They may either answer truthfully (the GM must give a true answer, though it may be cryptic) or mark 1 Fatigue and gain a Guilty Tell Condition (–1 die to all social rolls until they confess the truth to someone).
rites.push_it: The target must also reveal a surface emotion or a forgotten detail (GM's choice). Mark 1 SB (Hearts) as the Witness records the strain. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Echoing Truth
rites.materials: A reflective surface (mirror, still water, polished metal) used to focus on the target.
rites.effect: The target must make a Resolve test (DV 3) or suffer –1 die to rolls involving memory, deception, or resisting interrogation for the scene. If they fail, you may ask one specific, factual question about something they know, and they must answer truthfully or suffer 1 SB (Hearts) as the memory is forcibly drawn forth.
rites.push_it: If the target fails their Resolve test, you may ask a second question, but the mental intrusion causes them Harm 1 (Stress). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Immutable Record
rites.materials: A document signed by all parties within the zone, or a spoken pact witnessed by the caster.
rites.effect: Bind the agreement. Any party who knowingly breaches it suffers 1 SB (Hearts) immediately and gains a persistent Oathbreaker's Mark Condition (–1 die on social rolls involving honor, trust, or oaths until amends are made or a significant act redeems them).
rites.push_it: The bond becomes magically enforced for one specific, crucial clause: violation automatically inflicts Harm 1 (Stress) on the breaker in addition to the SB and Mark. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Shared Burden
rites.materials: A written secret (yours or another's) and a candle.
rites.effect: You transfer the weight of a truth. Choose one: you may remove a Guilty Tell, Haunted, or similar psychological Condition from yourself and give it to a willing or unwilling target (they resist with Resolve DV 4). Alternatively, you may share a secret with an ally; both of you clear 1 Fatigue as the burden is halved.
rites.push_it: Transfer a Condition without the target's consent (they automatically resist, but on failure they gain it). Mark 1 SB (Spades) as the secret stains them. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Unveiled Heart
rites.materials: A private setting where the target feels safe or is speaking freely.
rites.effect: The target suffers –2 dice to all attempts to conceal true emotions, intentions, or lies for the scene. Any successful social roll (Sway, Command, Deceit) made by the target generates 1 SB (Hearts) as the effort to maintain falsehoods under the Witness's gaze creates internal discord.
rites.push_it: You may designate one specific, complex question about the target's motivations, fears, or hidden loyalties. If you successfully use Sway or Insight against them this scene, you automatically learn the answer to that question. The intense scrutiny marks 1 SB (Spades) for you as the Witness's attention lingers. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Final Reckoning
rites.materials: A formally called gathering (court, council, family meeting) within the consecrated zone.
rites.effect: All present must speak their greatest debt, wrongdoing, or hidden truth related to the gathering's purpose. Those who lie or withhold suffer Harm 2 (Stress/Reputation). Truth-tellers gain +2 dice to social actions for the remainder of the scene within the zone.
rites.push_it: The truth becomes inescapable—even indirect lies or evasions related to the core topic suffer the Harm 2 penalty. The absolute nature of the revelation creates 2 SB (Diamonds) as the disruption to fates and secrets resonates. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of the Witness sings in truth-tolling—clear, piercing melodies that cut through evasion, harmonies that make the hidden surface. Their voice is used to compel a confession, to sound an alarm that a secret is about to be spoken, or to sing a historical record into being, each note a word that will not come unsaid. The Witness's Cantors are often found in courtrooms, in archive vaults, and at the bedsides of the dying, singing the last truth.

cult.name: The Congregation of the Unmasking
cult.description: The most feared of the Witness's cults, the Congregation of the Unmasking believes that the world will end when the last hidden truth is finally revealed—and that this ending is not a catastrophe but a liberation. They seek to expose every lie, every buried crime, every forgotten promise, no matter the cost. A ritual of the Congregation involves each member speaking aloud a truth they have kept secret, then burning a representation of the lie that concealed it. Their creed is painted on a scroll that is never fully unrolled: 'When all that is hidden is seen, the world will either break or be free. We will be there to witness which.' Outsiders are not welcome; they are potential sources of truth—or obstacles to be unmasked. The Congregation has been known to destroy families, topple governments, and start wars in their pursuit of total revelation. They are loved by none and feared by all, but even their enemies cannot deny that they are right: some secrets truly are worth dying to expose.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Record
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with the Witness is a ledger-scribe or seal-breaker—one who crafts the tools of permanent record: a book that cannot be altered once written, a quill that writes in ink that fades only when the truth it records is fulfilled, or a press that stamps each page with a sigil of authenticity. Their magic works through the materials of documentation: a chisel that carves a truth into stone so that it cannot be erased, a needle that sews a confession into a garment so that the wearer cannot deny it, or a forge that tempers a door that can only be opened by someone who has never told a lie.
witchcraft.lore: The ledger-scribe's path is the art of memory. They learn that every truth is a weight and every lie is a stain. To serve the Witness is to accept that you will never be loved—but you will never be deceived.
witchcraft.quote: Truth is not a gift. It is a burden.

quill_of_unwritten_truths.name: The Quill of Unwritten Truths
quill_of_unwritten_truths.description: A quill carved from a raven's feather, its nib dipped in ink made from lampblack and a drop of the witch's blood. Once per session, the witch may write a single sentence on a piece of parchment, then seal it with a drop of wax. For the next day, anyone other than the witch who reads the sentence must make a Resolve test (DV 3) or forget it immediately after reading. The witch may also use the quill to 'seal' a spoken secret, causing the speaker's voice to catch if they try to repeat it for the rest of the scene.

hedge_gifts.name: Record of a Breath
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may hold a blank piece of parchment up to a person's lips as they speak. The parchment absorbs the spoken words, recording them exactly as they were said—including tone, hesitation, and any unconscious meaning. The parchment can be read by anyone (the words appear in the speaker's own handwriting), but it crumbles to dust after being read aloud. The witch may also use this ability to record the final words of the dying, preserving them for one day.

hedge_gifts.name: The Truth-Teller's Eye
hedge_gifts.description: When you look into someone's eyes, you may ask the GM one yes/no question about a lie they are currently telling. The GM must answer truthfully, but the question must be specific (e.g., 'Are they lying about where they were last night?'). Once per scene.

hedge_gifts.name: The Unforgotten Name
hedge_gifts.description: Once per session, you may perfectly recall any name, face, or detail you have ever seen or heard. This does not grant new knowledge—only perfect memory of what you have already experienced.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Unmasked Fist
monastic_tradition.description: I will show you what you would rather forget. Unmasked Fists understand that truth is a weapon—and that the truth teller is never loved. They are archivists of the uncomfortable, witnesses to the truths that others would kill to keep hidden. To walk this path is to accept that some truths are weapons, and that the weight of memory is a burden that only grows heavier.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Spirit 3+, Wits 2+, Rite of the Lingering Trace or Cantor of The Witness.
monastic_tradition.quote: I will show you what you would rather forget.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Witness records, but does not collect. Monks of the Unmasked Fist gain +1 die to resist any magical debt or obligation that would force them to conceal the truth or perjure themselves. If they succeed, the creditor's ledger will show a blank where their name should be.

basic.name: Lingering Trace
basic.effect: Follow a hidden thread. Gain +1 die to investigate a specific trace within the current scene.

advanced.name: Shared Burden
advanced.effect: Transfer a psychological Condition (Guilty, Haunted) from yourself to a target (Resist DV 4) or share a secret with an ally to clear 1 Fatigue each.

master.name: Absolute Witness
master.effect: Once per session, become living truth for one scene: all deceptions within Near range automatically fail. You may demand a single truthful answer to one question from any creature, and they cannot refuse (no resistance roll) as long as the question pertains to the current scene or the target's immediate knowledge.
master.cost: After the scene, you gain a permanent Debt Scar (your eyes reflect light like a brass mirror) and may ignore one debt or obligation that would require you to lie—the creditor sees only the truth of your refusal.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Truth's Sight: +1 die to Insight when detecting deception or hidden motives.
corruption.cost: Burden of Knowledge: –1 die to social rolls involving lies or deception; others become uncomfortable with your piercing gaze.

corruption.benefit: Memory's Keeper: Once/scene, recall one specific detail from a previous scene with perfect clarity.
corruption.cost: Compulsive Honesty: Must correct obvious falsehoods witnessed, even when tactically disadvantageous.

corruption.benefit: Revelation's Power: +2 dice to rolls involving exposing secrets, uncovering lies, or forcing confessions.
corruption.cost: Truth-Blind: Suffer 1 Fatigue when exposed to comforting lies or willful ignorance.

corruption.benefit: Witness's Authority: Once/session, force one target to make a Resolve test (DV 4) or reveal a significant hidden truth.
corruption.cost: Isolation: –1 die to rolls requiring trust or close relationships; others fear your ability to uncover their secrets.

corruption.benefit: Omniscient Gaze: Once/session, see through all deceptions and lies for one exchange, gaining +3 dice to related actions.
corruption.cost: Paranoia: –1 die to rolls involving personal peace or rest; the weight of all truths witnessed creates constant mental strain.

corruption.benefit: Absolute Witness: Once/session, become the living embodiment of truth. For one scene, all deceptions within Near range automatically fail.
corruption.cost: Truth's Prison: Mark +3 Obligation when using this power; become unable to tolerate any form of deception, making normal social interaction nearly impossible. The Unmasking Beckons: The apocalyptic urge grows—you may be called to expose a truth that will destroy a community, a nation, or yourself.

playstyle_notes.description: The Witness rewards curiosity, patience, and a willingness to bear uncomfortable knowledge. Her followers are not merely investigators but archivists of the real—they record what others would erase. The Witness does not demand that you expose every secret; she simply ensures that you cannot forget the ones you learn. Intrusions often take the form of dreams showing a hidden crime, a sudden memory of a lie you told years ago, or the appearance of a scrap of parchment containing a truth you wish you had never read. High-Tier followers may find that secrets begin to seek them out—people confess unprompted, documents fall open to damning pages, and the world becomes a book that cannot be closed.
emphasizes: Truth as Burden: every secret known is a weight carried
Investigation as Ritual: uncovering lies is a sacred act
Memory as Weapon: forgetting can be as powerful as remembering
The Unmasking: exposing a truth can be an act of mercy or destruction
Witness as Isolation: those who know too much are seldom loved

sample_adventure.title: The Truth That Burns
sample_adventure.description: A powerful noble has been murdered, and the party is hired to investigate. But every clue leads to a dead end—until they discover that the noble was killed to protect a secret that could topple a kingdom. The party must decide: expose the secret and risk war, or bury it and become complicit in the very lies they swore to reveal. The Witness watches, and she will not forget which path they choose.
sample_adventure.quote: I will show you what you would rather forget. But first, you must forget what you think you know.

appears_in_religions.note: Invoked with the Oath of Flame & Light over the lamps and the texts.
Invoked with the Pale Shepherd over the Roll of the Drowned.

orders_are_masks: An Order is the shape this Patron takes inside a religion — the office through which it is approached, named and made respectable. The same Patron therefore appears in faiths that despise each other, and rarely at the same rank.

guises.name: The Ink-Eye
guises.note: A small eye is drawn on the inside of a scroll's wrapper, where a casual inspection will not find it. Some clerks copy a redacted passage there. Others keep only enough information to establish where a suppressed document once stood. Neither practice promises safety for the clerk or agreement about when the copy should be produced.

guises.name: The Fractured Mirror
guises.note: A fragment of mirror accompanies a sealed report. Spies use it to acknowledge that what they saw was partial, although ambitious patrons sometimes display a whole reconstructed mirror as proof of complete knowledge. A report can be accurate in every particular and misleading in what its commissioner refused to ask.

guises.among: Mistland communities after a bell-line failure
guises.name: The Fog-Scribe
guises.note: Identifying the dead can require a private fact as well as a face. Keepers hear the fact from someone willing to recognize the person publicly. Families sometimes ask them to preserve the identification while withholding how it was established. The Fog-Scribe's following includes people whom the truth has reunited and people frightened by the other truths it could release.

guises.name: The Uncovered Measure
guises.note: A covered measure is uncovered only after the official account has been recited. The gesture has been adopted by petitioners who want a disputed distribution compared with what was actually delivered. The scale does ordinary work; it is no universal judge of honesty. The divine witness may be invoked by the inspector, the complaining household, or both.

provenance.origin: The Witness is approached wherever an account survives pressure to replace it. Her followers' histories do not require one original tribunal to have authorized all later testimony.
provenance.summary: Many copying circles began as precautions against a familiar abuse: a revised order, a missing name, a memorial from which the defeated had disappeared. Their founders sometimes kept the evidence for years before allowing anyone to use it. Later Congregations of the Unmasking have claimed those predecessors as fearless public accusers, quietly shortening the long interval in which concealment was what kept the account alive.
provenance.the_migration: Displaced clerks carried copies into new offices; travelers brought names to the families that could identify them; investigators learned to compare a court's record with a household's mementos. In Oshiira, petitioners adapted this practice to disputes over material distributions rather than importing a foreign court's entire procedure. Vhasian intelligence households valued the same discipline for less public purposes.
provenance.why_it_took: Preserved evidence gives people leverage against an account already accepted by authority. Its keeper can therefore acquire authority of their own. A person who controls the only surviving copy may become the one everybody must please before the truth can be heard. Other followers make several copies, arrange witnesses, or put the decision back with the person whose account they preserved. Each choice creates different risks.
provenance.note: The Apocalyptic Witness is an interpretation pursued by the Congregation of the Unmasking, not a certainty every follower shares. Some keepers believe revelation must be immediate. Others refuse to destroy a speaker's chance of survival merely to make a truth public sooner. Their disagreement can continue even after everyone agrees about what happened.

philosophy.name: What the Truth Allows Its Keeper
philosophy.summary: Evidence may establish an event. It does not grant its possessor unlimited authority over everyone the event touched.
philosophy.the_point: A keeper can preserve another person's testimony faithfully and still use its release as a threat. The accuracy of the account does not make every use of it an act of justice.
philosophy.the_third_thing: Followers sometimes place their own contribution to a wrong beside the evidence against a more powerful person. The confession may weaken their standing in court. Omitting it would make the preserved account easier to deploy and less complete.
philosophy.at_the_table: A copy proves an official widened a punishment beyond the order they received. It also identifies the person who secretly warned the victims. Let the party test authenticity, prepare protection, negotiate a hearing, or expose a limited part without falsifying the rest. Avoid treating the widest possible disclosure as the automatic measure of courage.
